data.description:
# Generating-only pool with prefill-aware guard — Intake brief

## Problem statement
The proxy counts every in-flight local request toward `session_slot_pool_size`, so prefill and post-stream inactive holds can make the pool read as full while llama-server has 0 active streams. In the audited 2026-08-28 → 2026-08-29 window, 290/381 (76.1%) `local_concurrency_limit` fallbacks were during idle llama-server periods — false-full dispatches that unnecessarily push traffic to remote.

## Users
- Proxy operators / cost owners who need fewer false-full local fallbacks without regressing latency or availability.
- Session users whose requests are routed locally when a slot is actually generating vs. queued behind a prefill-only hold.

### User stories
- As an operator, I want only generating requests to occupy the local pool so idle-time `local_concurrency_limit` fallbacks drop measurably in the next proxy-usage window.
- As a client, I want TTFT to stay neutral or improve when the guard prevents over-subscribing prefills against `parallel=3`.
- As a maintainer, I want `session_slot_pool_size` to remain the single source of truth and cheap-mode contention-queue semantics to stay intact.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pool occupancy counts only generating slots toward `session_slot_pool_size`; during prefill and immediately after stream end the slot is not counted as full (no 30s inactive hold for non-generating).
- Prefill-aware guard prevents dispatch when concurrent prefills would saturate `parallel` (or slot_busy/n_past liveness), with no TTFT regression under `parallel=3` saturation in tests.
- `session_slot_pool_size` remains single source (`LP-0MTCZ35X7009IZKE`); cheap-mode bounded contention queue invariants (`LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D` / `LP-0MSOZF399000NV6I`) preserved.
- Unit tests for generating-only occupancy + prefill guard plus regression coverage; existing suites green (proxy, contention-queue, dispatch gate).
- `increment→first-byte` observability added (dispatch→first chunk measure) so follow-up audits can derive the distribution without request-ID correlation.
- Proxy-usage-window or benchmark quantification shows reduction in idle-time `local_concurrency_limit` fallbacks vs. the 290 baseline.

## Constraints
- Do not regress contention-queue invariants (fast mode is 99.2% of lcl; queue not the contributor).
- Do not fork `session_slot_pool_size`; keep derivation via `_get_local_max_concurrent_queries` / `_get_local_concurrency_info`.
- Adaptive prefill lease (60 + tokens*0.015 cap 1500s + prefill-progress) stays for in-flight prompts; narrowing is to generation-only occupancy.
- Orphan-cleanup coverage must remain (LP-0MSUO6HLX etc.).
- Any helper under `proxy/benchmarks/` is harness-only, not production routing.

## Existing state
- `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` / `_get_local_concurrency_info` gate on `local_active_queries >= session_slot_pool_size` and inactive-lease occupancy; `local_active_queries` increments at dispatch and decrements with a post-stream inactive hold; `_increment→first-byte` latency not derivable without request-ID correlation.
- Evidence window 2026-08-28 13:14:52 → 2026-08-29 13:14:52: 1293 fallbacks, 381 `local_concurrency_limit`, 290 idle-time (report + fast_sessions/cheap_sessions/errors CSVs, llama-server eval timing, proxy rotation logs).

## Desired change
- Make pool occupancy generating-only: hold the slot from first-byte onward; release during prefill and on stream end.
- Add a prefill-aware guard (cap concurrent prefills to `parallel` or check `slot_busy`/`n_past` liveness) before dispatch.
- Add `increment→first-byte` timing (dispatch to first chunk in `stream_generator`) for observability.
- Tests and doc updates (`docs/llama-router.md` if pool semantics change).

## Key Files
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — Change occupancy logic in `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` / `_increment/_decrement_local_active_queries` to generating-only; add prefill guard and first-byte timing hook
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — Update `_get_local_concurrency_info` and any occupancy read to generating-only count
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — Wire dispatch→first-byte measure in `stream_generator` (`Stream started` vicinity)
- `proxy/tests/test_local_dispatch_gate.py` — Unit/regression tests for generating-only occupancy + guard
- `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue.py` — Regression: cheap-mode queue invariants
- `docs/llama-router.md` — Document updated pool semantics if changed

## Related work
- Investigation `LP-0MTED3OLC001RJN4` T1 `LP-0MTH4FVFA000QAOK`, T2 `LP-0MTH4FZ9G002NVK6`, T3 `LP-0MTH4FZIO0060ACA` and comments `LP-C0MTH6TYQC008RNUD`, `LP-C0MTH74FZL005NZ8B`, `LP-C0MTH7A92Q008XJ4T`, `LP-C0MTH7DYFU004UZOP`
- Invariants `LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D`, `LP-0MSOZF399000NV6I` (contention queue), `LP-0MTCZ35X7009IZKE` (single source), `LP-0MTBTCK2I005MOTE` (post-rollout monitoring)
- Levers 2/3 follow-ups (lease shortening, KV reuse) deferred; parallel tracks `LP-0MTAQNB7J0094X71`, `LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM`

## Risks & assumptions
- Risk: Guard too permissive → llama-server internal queue saturation, TTFT regression. Mitigation: cap prefills to `parallel`, gate on slot_busy, benchmark under saturation.
- Risk: Guard too strict → no fallback reduction. Mitigation: tune and validate against 290 baseline; make cap observable.
- Risk: Regression of lease/queue semantics. Mitigation: preserve existing lease timeout + queue policy; targeted unit/integration tests.
- Risk: `increment→first-byte` without request-ID correlation remains noisy. Mitigation: emit dispatch and first-byte timestamps with correlation id in stream path.
- Assumption: `parallel=3` live aligns with `session_slot_pool_size=3`; window report data remain the baseline; no production lever change in this intake item itself.
- Scope creep: Lever 2 (post-stream lease 30s→5–10s) and Lever 3 (KV reuse) are separate follow-ups, not in scope here.

## Open Questions
- Prefill guard signal priority: slot_busy/n_past liveness vs. simple concurrent-prefill cap — which minimal signal is sufficient for first cut? (Default: cap to `parallel`, iterate.)
- Where to emit `increment→first-byte` (router vs. router_helpers) for minimal churn while keeping correlation stable?

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers
- No interview conducted — intake auto-drafted from the work-item's existing description and linked investigations (`LP-0MTED3OLC001RJN4` family). No assumptions beyond what is documented in the work item; any ambiguity flagged as Open Questions above.
data.title: Implement generating-only pool with prefill-aware guard to reduce false-full fallbacks
